headline: Nvidia Earnings in Focus as Market Braces for AI Results
body: Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) shares were under pressure ahead of its fiscal fourth-quarter earnings report, with investors anxious about the outlook for artificial intelligence spending. The chipmaker’s results could have major implications for the broader tech sector, as signs of risk to Nvidia’s long-held dominance have emerged. Despite AI companies facing market concerns, analysts at Citi reiterated a buy rating on the tech giant, noting that the valuation looks attractive and the stock is likely to outperform in the second half of 2026. The company’s gross margin could be under pressure due to higher costs for memory, but customers have indicated plans to boost AI infrastructure spending this year.

headline: Cava Group Soars on Strong Earnings, Growth Outlook
body: Shares of Mediterranean fast-casual restaurant chain CAVA Group (CAVA) jumped 20.7% in morning trading after the company reported fourth-quarter results that topped Wall Street’s expectations for revenue and earnings per share. The company guided to roughly 74–76 new restaurant openings and 3–5% same-store sales growth for 2026, laying out an aggressive growth plan that investors found appetizing. Management called out ongoing menu innovation and operational improvements as key drivers of the positive outlook. The results came as the broader restaurant sector continues to benefit from consumers trading up to premium dining experiences despite inflationary pressures.

headline: CoStar Group Falls on Soft Q1 Guidance
body: Shares of online real estate marketplace provider CoStar Group (CSGP) fell 8% after the company issued first-quarter guidance that fell short of expectations. CoStar called for adjusted earnings in the range of 16 to 19 cents per share, below analyst estimates. The guidance disappointment comes despite the company’s strong full-year 2025 performance, which included 19% revenue growth and adjusted EBITDA of $442 million, up 83% year-over-year. The company also announced a new $1.5 billion share repurchase program and $700 million in buybacks for 2026, signaling confidence in its long-term outlook despite the near-term headwinds.

headline: S&P 500 Gains on Tech Strength, Nvidia in Focus
body: The S&P 500 (SPY) edged higher as technology stocks led the market, with investors preparing for Nvidia’s earnings report later today. Redburn and other analysts reiterated buy ratings on the chipmaker, noting that the valuation looks attractive and the stock is likely to outperform in the second half of 2026. The market rally was also supported by positive labor market and economic reports, as well as Anthropic’s launch of new artificial intelligence integrations aimed at enterprise customers. However, concerns about the broader AI outlook and competitive pressures on Nvidia kept gains modest, with investors remaining cautious ahead of the highly anticipated earnings release.

headline: Anthropic’s Enterprise AI Push Boosts Software Sector
body: The software sector staged a comeback as Anthropic launched new artificial intelligence integrations aimed at enterprise customers, easing fears about AI’s impact on specialized software companies. The San Francisco-based AI lab’s expansion of Claude Cowork allows companies to connect the platform to existing tools like Google Drive and Gmail, while installing customizable plugins across domains such as financial analysis and human resources. This development has provided a much-needed “reality check” for the AI hype cycle, with investors now understanding how these technologies coexist rather than replace existing software solutions. The news helped lift major averages as software stocks rebounded from recent pressure.
